report:
Reviewed the complete book_explorer claim and both ordinary implementation entries, four ordinary tests and the explicit TODO test. Requirements are: a built explorer with model and Rust snapshots; embedded and full-page views; preserved handwritten links to searchable/interlinked Sage subchapters; shared rendering for book and local serve; browsing/source display without sage-meta serve; rebuild refresh after model or Rust changes.

Implementation: book.rs preprocess loads the current model, validates it, generates crate/module children, and writes sage-explorer.html into the configured book source. chapter/explorer_frame emit the iframe and full-page URL with depth-correct relative asset paths and encoded routes. generate_crates changes children without overwriting landing prose; render_sections renders its source links. The captured real Crates README contains the curated Sage links. browser.rs render_book_browser and render_browser_with_workspace both call render with the same Document model; captured main.rs routes local serving through the latter. render embeds model JSON, source_data's indexed Rust text/locations, CSS and JavaScript into one HTML asset. Captured browser.js reads those inline datasets, builds scoped entity maps, renders typed links and declaration/method views, filters search in memory, and populates the source pane from sources.files; it does not fetch code from a Sage server. Its navigation handles embedded and standalone views, and missing source explicitly. index.html supplies the matching controls and snapshot label. Rebuilds load fresh .sage contents and a new correspondence index that reads Rust files, so model and Rust changes reach the serialized snapshot; equal output avoids an unnecessary asset rewrite.

Tests: generates_crate_and_module_chapters_for_both_mdbook_protocols explicitly checks both supported protocols, generated hierarchy, iframe/full-page controls, relative asset URL and actual asset existence. curated_crates_landing_preserves_prose_and_links_to_generated_chapters checks exact retained prose apart from .sage-to-.html links, entity fragment retention, crate/module child placement, guide links and home navigation configuration. book_asset_is_self_contained_and_embeds_exact_script_safe_model_and_source parses embedded model, source and book datasets and compares exact model prose/Rust text and correspondence path; it also rejects external JS/CSS and unsubstituted placeholders. unchanged_preprocessing_preserves_asset_timestamp_and_source_edits_refresh_it checks byte and timestamp stability and changed model text appearing in both asset and chapter after rebuild. Fixture, recursive chapter extraction and script JSON parser are captured dependencies; assertions are visible in test bodies.

The fifth test, todo::self_contained_book_explorer, remains an honest deferred integration scenario, not execution evidence: its empty body explicitly calls for building and browsing embedded/full-page output with Rust source without a Sage server and refreshing after source changes. The ordinary tests now cover structural delivery, exact source embedding and model refresh, but do not drive a real browser or a Rust-only edit/rebuild lifecycle. Completing that TODO requires a browser harness opening a built book with no Sage process, exercising search/navigation/source controls in both presentations and observing model and Rust edits after rebuilding. The TODO continues to account for that runtime integration gap; no N/A entries are present. Source inspection supports the implementation and did not identify a concrete behavioral contradiction.

Execution: cargo fmt completed; cargo test -p sage-meta --test book passed all 13 tests, including a rerun after the coordinated curated-landing assertions changed; cargo build -p sage-meta passed. No browser runtime or mdbook publication run is claimed by this review. Added only an essential browser.rs implementation association and four existing substantive test associations, then restarted and captured fresh inputs. Central delegated post-codegen and Sage sanity checks remain the coordinator's separate change-completion checks.
